description.narrative: Depict the actual steps, or initiatives for steps taken by dutybearers to implement recommendations from UN Treaty Bodies where they are issued.

comment.narrative: There were no recommendations implemented at the beginning of the project.

Under the assumption that GoSoP remains committed to implement human rights standards in the national legal system and policy this indicator will describe the level of commitment and actual implementation.

Palestine has made limited progress in the implementation of received Recommendations upon the review under three of the seven applicable UN Human Rights treaties. Namely progress was made with the publication of CERD and CRC in the Official Gazette which enabled their direct application in the national legal order. Another progress noted is that the government has either drafted or initiated the drafting of Action Plans to followup on the Recommendations by Treaty Bodies. Such plans are ready for CEDAW and in progress for CERD and CRC. There still remain recommendations.

title.narrative: 1.1. Proportion of recommendations from the UN human rights mechanisms integrated in policies and programmes by the responsible Government entities.

description.narrative: 1.1. Proportion of recommendations from the UN human rights mechanisms integrated in policies and programmes by the responsible Government entities. Narrative assessment of national policies and programmes, including steps taken to integrate recommendations.

comment.narrative: At the start of the project there were no policies and programmes containing recommendations by UN human rights mechanisms.
The assessment of this target will also include initiatives and commitment taken by dutybearers to respond to recommendations by UN HR mechanisms.

Publishing CERD and CRC in the Official Gazette was a step forward for the integration of their provisions in domestic law. However it yet remains to be seen how the executive and judiciary will apply the human rights enshrined therein. The Action Plan on CERD has been developed in a draft form and is pending inputs by civil society while the one on CRC is in a very early stage shared within government institutions only. There are strategic commitments by MoSD to further integrate CRC in the education system and pay specific attention to children with disabilities. CEDAWs implementation has noted limited progress despite its Action Plan being developed which is mostly owed to a popular resistance to integrate this Convention in the domestic legal order. Attempts to amend and harmonise with CEDAW laws related to womens rights e.g. family status law and penal code or to adopt a family protection law have not been realized. On a positive note MoWA has showed commitment to raise awareness on CEDAW and womens rights in line with the Recommendations. With support of OHCHR the Ministry was able to train members of gender units of various lineministries and the security sector. Further raising awareness of civil society WHRDs has continued with a heightened pace.

CEDAWs implementation has noted limited progress despite its Action Plan being developed which is mostly owed to a popular resistance to integrate this Convention in the domestic legal order. Attempts to amend and harmonise with CEDAW laws related to womens rights e.g. family status law and penal code or to adopt a family protection law have not been realized. On a positive note MoWA has showed commitment to raise awareness on CEDAW and womens rights in line with the Recommendations. With support of OHCHR the Ministry was able to train members of gender units of various lineministries and the security sector. Further raising awareness of civil society WHRDs has continued with a heightened pace.
